results.reason_for_recall: CareLink Clinic software version 4.4A includes a software defect in the Settings Calculator feature in which the calculation logic fails to use custom values entered by healthcare professionals (HCPs) for Total Daily Dose (TDD) or Long-acting insulin when calculating the Carb Ratio, Insulin Sensitivity Factor (ISF), and Max Recommended value for Rapid-acting insulin. Instead, the calculator continues to use the system-recommended values, resulting in incorrect rapid-acting insulin parameters. If an HCP or patient inputs these incorrect setting values into the patient's MiniMed Go app, the patient could deliver higher or lower insulin doses compared to their insulin needs, potentially leading to over/under delivery of insulin with a severity ranging from Catastrophic (death from severe hypoglycemia) to Minor (self-treatable hypoglycemia/hyperglycemia).
results.action:
On 9/11/2026, correction notices were mailed to the health care professional, and customer asking them to do the following:

The Customer was asked to do the following:
Immediately contact your Healthcare Provider (HCP) to confirm your insulin settings values.

Complete and return the confirmation form by visiting https://info.medtronicdiabetes.com/FA1587 

The health care professional was asked to do the following: If you provided diabetes treatment recommendations to patients based on custom Total Daily Dose(TDD) or long-acting insulin values entered into the CareLin Clinic Settings Calculator between: June 04, 2026, to June 08, 2026, please revisit those recommendations utilizing patients' individual CareLink reports.

Continue to follow up with those patients pursuant to your standard of care.

If you have further questions or need assistance, please call the firm's 24-Hour Technical Support line at 1-800-646-4633, option 1.

Product Description: The MiniMed Go app for iOS or MiniMed Go app for Android is compatible with the following
components:
" Simplera sensor
" Instinct sensor
" InPen smart insulin pen
" Apple Watch [Optional]

Continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) is a technology that allows you to continuously view
glucose values. The app uses an inserted Simplera sensor CGM or Instinct sensor CGM with
Bluetooth wireless technology that converts small amounts of glucose from the interstitial fluid
under the skin into an electronic signal. The sensors use that signal to provide sensor glucose (SG)
values to the MiniMed Go app on a compatible mobile device.

The app also provides alerts based on your SG levels and contains a user interface for entering data
such as insulin, meals, exercise, blood glucose (BG) values, and uploading information to the
CareLink" Personal website.
The app is available to download from the Apple"* App Store"* or the Google Play"* Store.

results.reason_for_recall: A software defect in which existing users who had previously configured and enabled the long-acting dose reminder feature in version 1.2.0 or earlier experienced failure of the long-acting dose reminder after updating their app to version 1.2.1. The long-acting dose reminder is an optional feature that, when enabled, triggers a notification at the scheduled time to remind users to take their long-acting insulin dose. The issue was caused by a type cast exception during database migration that occurs upon app update to version 1.2.1 causing a silent failure that prevented the creation of new alerts. Failure to receive the long-acting dose reminder may result in missed or delayed insulin doses, potentially leading to hyperglycemia. Conversely, if users are uncertain whether they took their dose due to the missing reminder, inadvertent duplicate dosing may occur, potentially resulting in hypoglycemia.
results.action:
On 09/14/2026, customers were contacted via SMS, emailed or via an "URGENT MEDICAL DEVICE CORRECTION" Letter informing them that, an issue was identified with the MiniMed Go app in which the long-acting dose reminders were not being delivered after the app was updated to version 1.2.1.

Actions required:
Users of MiniMed Go app software versions 1.2.1 should update to version 1.2.2 or higher as soon as possible to resolve this issue. This update will ensure enabled long-acting reminders are delivered as expected.
For iOS Users:
To confirm the latest app version on your iOS device, follow the steps below:
1. Open the App Store.
2. Tap your profile icon at the top of the screen.
3. Scroll to see pending updates.
4. Tap Update next to the MiniMed Go app icon.
For Android Users:

To confirm the latest app version on your Android device, follow the steps below:
1. Open the Google Play Store.
2. Tap Menu, then select Manage apps & device.
3. Apps with an update available are labeled  Update available.  You can also search for theMiniMed Go app.
4. Tap Update next to the MiniMed Go app icon.

For Questions or assistance - call the Medtronic MiniMed 24-Hour Technical Support line at 1-800-646-4633, option 1.
